paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God has spoken, and the clearest word He ever gave us is His Son. He spoke through the prophets on many past occasions, but "in these last days He has spoken to us by His Son" (Hebrews 1:2). The Son is "the radiance of God's glory and the exact representation of His nature, upholding all things by His powerful word" (Hebrews 1:3). So when you want to know what God is like, you don't squint at the clues, you look at Jesus.

And the writer wants you to see how high Jesus stands. Not one angel ever heard "You are My Son" (Hebrews 1:5), and God even says, "Let all God's angels worship Him" (Hebrews 1:6). The angels are "ministering spirits sent to serve those who will inherit salvation" (Hebrews 1:14), which means they're serving YOU, baker! The earth and the heavens will wear out, but of the Son it says "You remain the same, and Your years will never end" (Hebrews 1:12). That's a Savior who is not going anywhere.

So here's why it matters to you today. "We must pay closer attention, therefore, to what we have heard, so that we do not drift away" (Hebrews 2:1). Nobody plans to drift, friend, it just happens one quiet day at a time. That's why the writer asks, "how shall we escape if we neglect such a great salvation?" (Hebrews 2:3), and why God confirmed it with "signs, wonders, various miracles, and gifts of the Holy Spirit" (Hebrews 2:4). Keep your eyes on the Son, keep listening, and keep your ovens ready.
